senses.def: used before a noun when the listener already knows which person or thing you mean
ex: Can you open the window, please?
I left the keys on the kitchen table.

senses.def: used before a noun when there is only one of something in the world
ex: The sun is very hot today.
She wants to travel around the world.

senses.def: used before superlative adjectives and words like first, last and only
ex: This is the best pizza in town.
He was the first person to arrive at the party.

senses.def: used before an adjective to talk about a whole group of people
ex: The charity collects warm clothes for the poor.
Big cities are not always easy places for the elderly.

senses.def: to move or travel from one place to another
ex: We go to the beach every summer.
Shall we go by train?

senses.def: to leave home or another place in order to do an activity
ex: Let’s go swimming this afternoon.
They went for a walk after dinner.

senses.def: to leave a place
ex: I have to go now, it’s getting late.
Has the last bus gone already?

senses.def: to become different, usually in a bad way
ex: The milk has gone bad.
Everything went wrong on the first day of our holiday.

senses.def: to happen or develop in a particular way
ex: How did your job interview go?
The party went really well, and everyone enjoyed it.

senses.def: in a good, skilful or successful way
ex: She speaks Spanish very well.
Did you sleep well last night?

senses.def: also; too, used in the phrase "as ..." at the end of a sentence
ex: Can I have a glass of water as well?
My brother is coming to the wedding as well.

senses.def: completely, carefully or closely
ex: Shake the bottle well before you open it.
I know the city quite well now.

senses.def: by a large amount; much, used before words like above, over and before
ex: The repairs cost well over a thousand dollars.
We arrived well before the doors opened, so we got good seats.

senses.def: a lot; to a great degree, often used in negatives and questions
ex: Thank you very much for the flowers!
I don’t like spicy food much.

senses.def: a lot, used before comparative adjectives and before "too"
ex: Our new flat is much bigger than the old one.
This coat is much too expensive for me.

senses.def: often; a lot of the time, mainly in questions and negatives
ex: Do you go out much in the evenings?
We don’t see our cousins much now that they live abroad.

senses.def: to make letters, words or numbers on paper or a screen
ex: Write your answers in pencil.
My little boy is learning to write.

senses.def: to send a letter, email or message to someone
ex: I wrote a letter to my grandmother.
Please write me a short email.

senses.def: to create a book, story, song, article or other piece of work
ex: She has written three novels about her childhood.
Who wrote this song? It’s beautiful.

senses.def: coming straight after the present one in time or order
ex: I’ll see you next Monday.
The next train leaves at six.

senses.def: nearest in place to where you are now
ex: We get off at the next stop.
The music from the next room kept me awake.

senses.def: something you say or write to ask for information
ex: Can I ask you a question?
Please answer every question on the form.
pat: ask sb a question about sth

senses.def: a problem or matter that people need to discuss or deal with
ex: The meeting will discuss the question of parking near the school.
It’s only a question of time before prices go up again.

senses.def: doubt or uncertainty about whether something is true or right
ex: She is, without question, the best player on the team.
Nobody has ever called his honesty into question.

senses.def: the work of buying, selling or making things for money
ex: My aunt travels a lot on business.
Business is good this year.

senses.def: a company, shop or other organization that sells goods or services
ex: They run a small family business near the market.
Many local businesses closed after the floods.

senses.def: something that concerns only a particular person and not other people
ex: How much I earn is none of your business.
What I do at the weekend is my own business.

senses.def: to show someone the way by going in front of them
ex: The guide led us through the old town.
She led the children safely across the road.

senses.def: to cause something to happen or to make someone do something
ex: Too much stress can lead to health problems.
The discovery led to a new treatment for the disease.

senses.def: to be in charge of a group, team, activity or organization
ex: She leads a team of ten engineers.
Who will lead the discussion at tomorrow’s meeting?

senses.def: if a road, path or door leads somewhere, it goes there
ex: This road leads to the airport.
A narrow path led down to the beach.

senses.def: to live a particular kind of life
ex: My grandparents led a simple life in the countryside.
Despite his illness, he leads a normal, active life.

senses.def: having the skill, strength, time or chance to do something
ex: Will you be able to help me tomorrow?
I wasn’t able to sleep because of the noise.

senses.def: clever or good at doing something
ex: She is a very able student who learns quickly.
The project needs an able and experienced manager.

senses.def: to have the power to decide how a person, organization, machine or system works
ex: Who controls the company now?
You can control the lights with your phone.

senses.def: to limit something or stop it from increasing or spreading
ex: Firefighters worked all night to control the fire.
The city wants to control traffic in the centre.

senses.def: to stay calm and stop yourself from showing strong feelings
ex: Try to control your temper when you’re tired.
He couldn’t control his laughter during the speech.

senses.def: energy, especially electricity, used to make machines and lights work
ex: There was no power after the storm.
Turn off the power before you change the light bulb.

senses.def: the ability to control people, events or a country
ex: The president has a lot of power.
The party came to power after the election.

senses.def: a natural ability or strength to do something
ex: Some people believe music has the power to heal.
She lost the power of speech after the accident.

senses.def: a country with a lot of military or economic influence
ex: The summit brought together the world’s leading powers.
After the war, the country became a major economic power.

senses.def: an area of knowledge that you study at school
ex: Science is my favourite subject.
Which subjects do you study?

senses.def: the thing that people are talking or writing about
ex: Let’s change the subject.
Climate change is the subject of her new book.

senses.def: in grammar, the noun or pronoun that usually comes before the verb and does the action
ex: In the sentence ‘She sings’, the subject is ‘she’.
Every English sentence needs a subject and a verb.

senses.def: a person or thing that is being studied, painted or photographed
ex: All the subjects in the study were over sixty.
Her cat is the subject of most of her photographs.

senses.def: one of the two parts of the face that you see with
ex: She has big brown eyes.
Close your eyes and relax.

senses.def: careful attention or watching, so that you notice what happens
ex: Can you keep an eye on my bag for a minute?
A bright red poster caught my eye in the shop window.

senses.def: an ability to notice and judge what is good, attractive or important
ex: She has a great eye for colour.
You need an eye for detail to work as an editor.

senses.def: the whole system of rules that people in a country must obey
ex: Stealing is against the law.
Everyone has to obey the law, including the police.

senses.def: one official rule made by a government
ex: The government passed a new law on plastic bags.
There is a law against smoking in restaurants.

senses.def: the study of legal rules as a university subject or profession
ex: My sister is studying law at university.
He went to law school after working as a teacher.

senses.def: a statement that describes what always happens in nature or science
ex: The laws of physics explain why objects fall to the ground.
Supply and demand is one of the basic laws of economics.

senses.def: completely sure that something is true or correct
ex: Are you certain you turned off the oven?
I’m not certain what time the film starts.

senses.def: sure to happen or to be true; definite
ex: It’s almost certain that it will rain tomorrow.
With their best player injured, the team is certain to lose.

senses.def: used to talk about a particular person, thing or amount without saying exactly which
ex: The museum is closed on certain days of the week.
Certain foods can cause allergies in young children.

senses.def: to make a picture with a pencil, pen or crayon
ex: Can you draw a cat?
He drew a map for me.

senses.def: to finish a game with the same score as the other player or team
ex: The two teams drew one–one.
We drew with the champions last weekend, which was a great result.

senses.def: to attract people, or to attract their interest or attention
ex: The festival draws thousands of visitors every year.
She tried not to draw attention to herself.

senses.def: to decide what is true or compare things after thinking about the facts
ex: It’s too early to draw any conclusions from the results.
The writer draws a comparison between city and village life.

senses.def: to have a particular opinion about someone or something
ex: Many people regard her as the best writer of her generation.
The old bridge is widely regarded as a symbol of the city.

senses.def: to look carefully at someone or something, often in a particular way
ex: The guard regarded us with suspicion as we walked past.
The cat sat on the wall, regarding the birds calmly.

senses.def: actions and systems used to protect people, buildings or a country from danger or crime
ex: There was tight security at the airport.
A security guard asked to see our tickets.

senses.def: the feeling of being safe, protected and free from worry
ex: Children need love and a sense of security.
Many workers value job security more than a high salary.

senses.def: protection of computers, networks and personal data from attack or theft
ex: Change your password regularly to improve your online security.
The company hired experts to test the security of its app.

senses.def: a substance such as wood, plastic or metal that things are made from
ex: This bag is made from recycled materials.
The builders are waiting for more material.

senses.def: cloth used for making clothes, curtains and other things
ex: I need two metres of soft cotton material for the dress.
This material is light and easy to wash.

senses.def: information or ideas used in lessons, books, films or other work
ex: The teacher prepares new material for every class.
This website has plenty of free study material.

senses.def: especially; more than usual or more than others
ex: I love fruit, particularly fresh mangoes.
The roads are particularly busy on Friday evenings.

senses.def: used after "not" to mean "not very" or "not much"
ex: I’m not particularly hungry right now.
The film wasn’t particularly good, but the music was great.

senses.def: able to move or travel at high speed
ex: This car is very fast.
She is the fastest runner in our class.

senses.def: happening or done in a short time
ex: The internet here is really fast.
Fast food is cheap but not very healthy.

senses.def: if a clock or watch is this, it shows a time later than the real time
ex: My watch is five minutes fast.
Don’t worry, that kitchen clock is always fast.

senses.def: a person in charge of a shop, business, department or group of workers
ex: The hotel manager apologized for the noise.
She became a sales manager last year.

senses.def: a person who trains and is in charge of a sports team
ex: The team’s manager was happy with the result.
The club has appointed a new manager for next season.

senses.def: a person who looks after the business side of a singer, actor or sports star
ex: The singer’s manager organized the whole world tour.
Her manager handles all her contracts and interviews.

senses.def: the goods that a shop or company has available to sell
ex: Sorry, we don’t have that model in stock at the moment.
The shop sold its entire stock of umbrellas in an hour.

senses.def: an amount of something that is kept or exists, ready to be used
ex: We keep a stock of bottled water at home in case of emergencies.
Fish stocks in the sea are falling fast.

senses.def: shares in a company, or the value of those shares
ex: She invested her savings in stocks and bonds.
Technology stocks rose sharply this morning.

senses.def: a liquid made by boiling meat, bones or vegetables, used to make soups and sauces
ex: Add a litre of vegetable stock and cook for twenty minutes.
Homemade chicken stock gives the soup a much richer taste.

senses.def: a chemical substance used as medicine to treat an illness
ex: The doctor gave me a drug for the pain.
Scientists are testing a new drug for flu.

senses.def: an illegal substance that people take for pleasure and can become addicted to
ex: The police found drugs hidden in the car.
Taking drugs can seriously damage your health.

senses.def: the flat surface of a room that you walk on
ex: The kitchen floor is wet.
Please put your bags on the floor.

senses.def: all the rooms on the same level of a building
ex: I live on the third floor.
The shoe shop is on the ground floor.

senses.def: the ground at the bottom of the sea, a forest or a valley
ex: Strange creatures live on the ocean floor.
Dry leaves covered the forest floor in autumn.

senses.def: a folded piece of stiff paper with a picture on the front and a message inside
ex: Did you get my birthday card?
We sent our teacher a thank-you card.

senses.def: a small piece of plastic from a bank, used to pay for things or get money
ex: Can I pay by card?
I lost my bank card yesterday.

senses.def: one of a set of small pieces of stiff paper with numbers and pictures, used for playing games
ex: Let’s play cards after dinner.
She mixed the cards and gave everyone seven.

senses.def: a small piece of stiff paper or plastic with your name and other details on it
ex: Here’s my business card with my phone number.
You need your student card to borrow books.

senses.def: medical care given to someone who is ill or injured
ex: She is receiving treatment for a back injury.
There is now an effective treatment for this disease.

senses.def: the way you behave towards someone or deal with them
ex: Everyone deserves fair treatment at work.
Why does he always get special treatment from the teacher?

senses.def: a process used to clean, protect or change a substance
ex: The water goes through several stages of treatment before it reaches our taps.
The wood has had a special treatment to protect it from insects.

senses.def: not including; but not
ex: I eat everything except mushrooms.
All the shops were closed except the bakery.

senses.def: used before the one thing that makes a statement not completely true, usually in "except for"
ex: The room was empty except for an old chair.
The essay is good, except for a few spelling mistakes.

senses.def: a very young child who cannot walk or talk yet
ex: The baby is crying again.
My sister had a baby last month.

senses.def: a very young animal
ex: The baby elephant stayed close to its mother.
In spring the garden is full of baby birds.

senses.def: the youngest person in a family or group
ex: She’s the baby of the family, so everyone spoils her.
At twenty, he was the baby of the team.

senses.def: to give an answer when you are not sure if it is right
ex: Guess what I bought today!
Can you guess her age?

senses.def: to think that something is probably true; to suppose
ex: I guess you’re right about the weather.
I guess we should leave before the traffic gets bad.

senses.def: something you decide is true after thinking carefully about all the facts
ex: We came to the conclusion that the house was too small for us.
What conclusions can we draw from these results?

senses.def: the last part of something such as an essay, speech or story
ex: In conclusion, I would like to thank everyone for coming.
The conclusion of the film was a big surprise.

senses.def: of the sex that can give birth to babies or produce eggs
ex: Female lions do most of the hunting.
The company wants more female managers.

senses.def: the process of sharing information, ideas or feelings with other people
ex: Good communication between parents and teachers helps children do well.
Problems in the team were caused by a lack of communication.

senses.def: ways of sending information, such as phones, radio and the internet
ex: The storm cut off all communications with the island for two days.
Satellites play an important role in global communication.

senses.def: a message, letter, email or phone call
ex: We have had no further communication from the company since March.
All written communication with the bank should include your account name.

senses.def: a little hot, in a pleasant way
ex: The water in the lake is warm.
Come and get warm by the fire.

senses.def: keeping you from feeling cold
ex: Take a warm coat because it’s cold outside.
These boots are light but very warm.

senses.def: friendly, kind and showing that you care about people
ex: They gave us a warm welcome.
My grandmother has a warm smile.

senses.def: without involving any other person, thing or place in between
ex: You can buy tickets directly from the theatre.
The new rules will directly affect small businesses.

senses.def: in a straight line or exactly in a particular position
ex: Go directly to the gate after the security check.
Our hotel is directly opposite the station.

senses.def: in an honest and clear way, saying exactly what you mean
ex: She asked him directly whether he wanted the job.
I prefer people who speak directly instead of hinting.

senses.def: added to what already exists or is already there; extra
ex: There is an additional charge for breakfast.
We need two additional chairs for the meeting.

senses.def: as good as it can be, with nothing wrong
ex: Your English is perfect!
It’s a perfect day for a picnic.

senses.def: exactly right for a particular person, purpose or situation
ex: This flat is perfect for a small family.
She is the perfect person for the job.

senses.def: complete, used to make a word stronger
ex: I’d never seen him before; he was a perfect stranger.
It makes perfect sense to book the tickets early.

senses.def: the quality of being hot, or a high temperature
ex: I can’t sleep in this heat.
The heat from the fire kept us warm all night.

senses.def: the level of temperature used when cooking something
ex: Cook the onions over a low heat until they are soft.
Turn up the heat and bring the water to the boil.

senses.def: one of the early races in a competition that decides who goes to the final
ex: She won her heat easily and reached the final.
He finished third in his heat and was out of the competition.

senses.def: a state of strong emotion or excitement, for example during an argument
ex: I said things in the heat of the moment that I later regretted.
In the heat of the argument, nobody was listening.
col: in the heat of the moment

senses.def: to try very hard to do something that is difficult
ex: Many families are struggling to pay their bills.
I always struggled with maths at school.

senses.def: to fight or move your body strongly, especially to get free
ex: The cat struggled to get out of my arms.
He struggled against the strong current and finally reached the shore.

senses.def: to move somewhere with great effort
ex: She struggled up the hill with her heavy shopping bags.
We struggled through the deep snow to the car.

senses.def: a round object that you throw, kick or hit in games
ex: The dog ran after the ball.
Throw me the ball, please!

senses.def: something that has been formed into a round shape
ex: Roll the dough into small balls.
The kitten played with a ball of wool.

senses.def: a large formal party where people dance
ex: They first met at a charity ball.
She wore a long silver dress to the ball.

senses.def: water that falls from clouds in small drops
ex: We waited for the rain to stop.
I got caught in the rain.

senses.def: the wet season in tropical countries, when water falls from the sky almost every day
ex: Farmers are waiting anxiously for the rains to arrive.
The roads often flood when the rains come.

senses.def: something you must do because it is morally or legally right
ex: Parents have a duty to protect their children.
I felt it was my duty to report the accident.
pat: have a duty to do sth

senses.def: a task that is part of your job
ex: Your duties will include answering the phone and greeting visitors.
The new manager took up her duties on Monday.

senses.def: the time when someone such as a nurse or police officer is working
ex: Which doctor is on duty tonight?
The nurse goes off duty at six in the morning.

senses.def: a tax that you pay on goods, especially goods brought into a country
ex: You have to pay duty on goods worth more than a certain amount.
We bought some chocolate at the duty-free shop.

senses.def: to advertise a product or event so that people buy it or go to it
ex: The band is touring to promote their new album.
Famous athletes are often paid to promote sports drinks.

senses.def: to help something develop, happen or become more common
ex: Regular exercise promotes good sleep.
Schools should promote respect between students.

senses.def: to move someone to a more important job or rank
ex: She was promoted to manager after two years.
He hopes to be promoted before the end of the year.

senses.def: to do something illegal or seriously wrong
ex: The police believe he committed the crime alone.
Most burglaries are committed during the day.

senses.def: to promise to do something, or to give your time and energy to it
ex: The government has committed to cutting pollution by half.
She is fully committed to her studies this year.

senses.def: to decide to use money, time or people for a particular purpose
ex: The city has committed millions to building new cycle lanes.
We can’t commit any more staff to the project until next year.

senses.def: to give someone the ability or chance to do something
ex: The new bridge will enable drivers to avoid the city centre.

senses.def: to make a feature or setting on a computer or phone start working
ex: Enable location services in your phone settings.
You must enable notifications to receive reminders from the app.

senses.def: a performance of music in front of an audience
ex: We went to a rock concert.
The concert starts at eight.

senses.def: the flavour that food or drink has in your mouth
ex: I love the taste of fresh strawberries.
This sauce has a slightly sweet taste.

senses.def: the sense that lets you recognize flavours in your mouth
ex: When I have a cold, I lose my sense of taste.
Smell and taste are closely connected.

senses.def: a small amount of food or drink that you try
ex: Can I have a taste of your soup?
Give the sauce a quick taste before you add more salt.

senses.def: the kind of things that a person likes, or the ability to choose things that look good
ex: We have very different tastes in music.
Their house is decorated with great taste.

senses.def: a shape with four straight sides that are all the same length
ex: Draw a square in the middle of the page.
Cut the bread into small squares.

senses.def: an open public space in a town, usually with buildings on all four sides
ex: The old town square fills with tourists in summer.
Let’s meet in the main square at noon.

senses.def: the number you get when you multiply a number by itself
ex: The square of four is sixteen.

senses.def: the line that divides two countries or areas
ex: We crossed the border by train early in the morning.
The town lies close to the northern border.

senses.def: a narrow strip along the edge of something, often as decoration
ex: The white plates have a thin blue border.
She planted roses along the border of the garden.

senses.def: one of the four long thin parts at the end of your hand, or five including the thumb
ex: She wears a gold ring on her little finger.
Don’t point your finger at people; it’s rude.
Cross your fingers for my exam tomorrow!

senses.def: to try to find out all the facts about something, such as a crime or an accident
ex: Police are investigating the robbery at the bank.
Engineers are investigating why the bridge collapsed.

senses.def: to study a subject carefully in order to discover new facts
ex: The study investigates how sleep affects memory.
Researchers investigated the effects of music on young children.

senses.def: to marry someone, used especially in newspapers
ex: The couple wed in a small ceremony last June.
They plan to wed next spring in her home town.

senses.def: to join two different qualities, ideas or things closely together
ex: The design weds traditional craft with modern technology.

senses.def: an official group of people who join together for a shared purpose or interest
ex: She joined the local residents’ association.

senses.def: a connection or working relationship between people or organizations
ex: The festival is organized in association with local businesses.
His long association with the club ended last year.

senses.def: a feeling, memory or idea that comes into your mind when you think of something
ex: For me, the smell of rain has happy associations with childhood.

senses.def: something that makes you feel proud because people respect you
ex: It’s a great honor to meet you.
It was an honor to play for my country.

senses.def: great respect and admiration shown to someone
ex: A ceremony was held in honor of the firefighters.
The festival is held in honor of the city’s founder.

senses.def: strong moral principles that make you behave honestly and fairly
ex: Her sense of honor would not let her lie.
He is a person of honor who always keeps his promises.

senses.def: an award or title given to someone for their achievements
ex: She received the country’s highest honor for her work.
The scientist has won many honors during her career.

senses.def: the act of going into a place, or the right to go into it
ex: Entry to the museum is free on Sundays.

senses.def: something that you send in to try to win a competition
ex: The winning entry was a photo of a tiny green frog.

senses.def: a separate item written in a dictionary, diary, list or online record
ex: Each dictionary entry gives examples of how the word is used.
I found her diary entry from the day we met.

senses.def: the act of becoming a member of a group or starting to take part in something
ex: Entry into the medical school is very competitive.
Check the entry requirements before you apply for the course.

senses.def: to ask for a seat, table, room or ticket to be kept for you to use later
ex: I’ve reserved a table for four at eight o’clock.

senses.def: to keep something for a particular person or purpose
ex: These parking spaces are reserved for disabled drivers.

senses.def: to officially keep a right or power for yourself, especially in legal notices

senses.def: a short funny story or something said to make people laugh
ex: My dad always tells terrible jokes.

senses.def: something that is said or done to be funny and is not meant seriously
ex: Don’t be angry; it was only a joke.
I said it as a joke, but she believed me.

senses.def: a person or thing that is so bad or silly that you cannot take it seriously
ex: The new bus timetable is a joke; the buses never arrive on time.

senses.def: connected with education, especially at schools, colleges and universities
ex: The academic year starts in September.
She has an excellent academic record.

senses.def: involving reading, studying and thinking rather than practical skills
ex: Some children are less academic but very good with their hands.
The course mixes academic subjects with work experience.

senses.def: having no practical importance because it cannot change what happens
ex: Since the shop has already closed, the question of price is purely academic.
Whether we could have won is now an academic question.

senses.def: to try to achieve something over a long period of time
ex: She left her job to pursue her dream of becoming a chef.
He wants to pursue a career in engineering.

senses.def: to follow someone or something in order to catch them
ex: Police pursued the stolen car through the city.

senses.def: to continue to discuss, find out about or be involved in something
ex: The police decided not to pursue the matter any further.

senses.def: the fixed amount of money you are paid for your job, usually every month

He earns a good salary as a nurse.

senses.def: the food and drink that you usually have every day

senses.def: a plan to eat less or only certain foods, to lose weight or for health
ex: I’m on a diet, so no cake for me.

senses.def: to fix something that is broken or damaged so that it works again
ex: Can you repair my bike by Friday?

senses.def: to improve a bad situation or a damaged relationship

senses.def: (British English) a long thin piece of potato fried in oil and eaten hot
ex: Can I have fish and chips, please?
These chips are too salty.

senses.def: (American English) a very thin, dry slice of fried potato, sold in packets
ex: We bought a bag of potato chips for the long drive.
Tortilla chips with salsa make a quick snack.

senses.def: a very small electronic part inside a computer or phone that controls how it works
ex: The new model has a faster chip than the old one.
Modern cars contain hundreds of computer chips.

senses.def: a small piece that has broken off something, or the mark it leaves
ex: There’s a chip in the rim of this cup.
Wood chips covered the floor of the workshop.

senses.def: happening very quickly and when you do not expect it
ex: There was a sudden noise from the kitchen.
The sudden rise in prices surprised everyone.
All of a sudden, the lights went out.

senses.def: an attempt by many people, often using violence, to change a country’s government
ex: The revolution ended three hundred years of royal rule.
Students played a key role in starting the revolution.

senses.def: a complete change in the way people live, work or think
ex: Online shopping has brought a revolution in how people buy things.
The digital revolution has changed almost every kind of job.

senses.def: one complete turn of an object around a central point
ex: The engine was running at three thousand revolutions per minute.
The Earth completes one revolution around the Sun every year.

senses.def: something good that you have done successfully, usually with effort or skill
ex: Finishing the marathon was her greatest achievement.
Winning the prize is a fantastic achievement for such a young team.

senses.def: the act or feeling of succeeding in something after working hard
ex: Hard work and good teaching both lead to higher academic achievement.
Learning to swim at sixty gave him a real sense of achievement.

senses.def: telling the truth and never cheating, lying or stealing
ex: She’s honest and hard-working, so everyone trusts her.
An honest taxi driver returned the wallet I had left in his car.

senses.def: saying what you really think, even if it is not pleasant to hear
ex: To be honest, I didn’t enjoy the film very much.
Can I give you my honest opinion about your essay?

senses.def: a narrow line on the surface of something where it has broken but not come apart
ex: My phone screen has a crack in the corner.
Cracks appeared in the walls after the earthquake.

senses.def: a narrow space between two things or two parts of something
ex: Light came through a crack in the curtains.
She opened the door a crack and looked out.

senses.def: a sudden short loud sound, like something hard breaking
ex: We heard a loud crack of thunder.
There was a crack as the branch broke.

senses.def: not true or not correct
ex: Is this sentence true or false?
That story is completely false.

senses.def: not real, but made to look real
ex: He gave the police a false name.
My grandfather wears false teeth.

senses.def: based on a wrong idea or belief
ex: The doctor did not want to give us false hope.
Everyone left the building, but luckily it was a false alarm.

senses.def: unhappy and sorry because you know you have done something wrong
ex: I felt guilty about eating all the chocolate.
Don’t feel guilty about taking a day off.

senses.def: having broken a law, or having done something wrong
ex: The jury found him guilty of theft.
She was found not guilty and walked free.

senses.def: to take money out of a bank account or cash machine
ex: I withdrew two hundred euros from the cash machine.
You can withdraw money at any of our branches.

senses.def: to stop taking part in an activity, competition or organization
ex: She withdrew from the race because of a knee injury.
Two candidates have withdrawn from the election.

senses.def: to take back something that you have offered, said or made available
ex: The company withdrew the product after customers complained.
He later withdrew his comments and apologized.

senses.def: to move soldiers or other people away from a place
ex: The army began to withdraw its troops from the region.
Both sides agreed to withdraw their forces from the border.

senses.def: a spoken or written request asking someone to come to a party, event or meal
ex: Did you get an invitation to her party?
We sent out fifty wedding invitations.

senses.def: something that makes it more likely that a particular thing, often a bad one, will happen
ex: Leaving your car unlocked is an open invitation to thieves.
Low prices are an invitation to customers to buy more than they need.

senses.def: a spirit or being that people believe has power over nature or part of life
ex: The ancient Greeks had a god of the sea.
In the story, the gods were angry with the king.

senses.def: in many religions, the one being who made and controls the world; written with a capital letter
ex: Do you believe in God?
Thank God nobody was hurt in the accident.

senses.def: made of only one substance, with nothing else added
ex: The ring is made of pure gold.
This juice is pure orange, with no added sugar.

senses.def: clean and free from anything harmful or dirty
ex: The spring water here is pure enough to drink.
We moved to the coast for the pure sea air.

senses.def: complete, used to make a noun stronger
ex: We met by pure chance at the airport.
It was pure luck that we found the keys.

senses.def: dealing only with theory, not with practical uses
ex: She studied pure mathematics at university.
The lab does both pure and applied research.

senses.def: either of the two soft edges at the top and bottom of your mouth
ex: My lips get dry in winter.
He bit his lip and tried not to laugh.

senses.def: the edge of a cup, jug or opening
ex: Coffee dripped from the lip of the jug.
She stood on the lip of the crater and looked down.

senses.def: the space between two lines or surfaces that meet, measured in degrees
ex: A square has four angles of ninety degrees.
The picture is hanging at an angle.

senses.def: a position from which you look at or photograph something
ex: The photographer took pictures of the building from every angle.
From this angle, you can see the whole valley.

senses.def: a particular way of thinking about a problem or situation
ex: Let’s look at the problem from a different angle.
Journalists are always looking for a new angle on the story.

senses.def: something that people in a particular place have done in the same way for a long time
ex: In many countries it is the custom to give gifts at New Year.
Every region has its own wedding customs.
pat: it is the custom (for sb) to do sth

senses.def: (customs) the place at a border where officials check your bags and goods
ex: It took us an hour to get through customs.
Customs officers searched our luggage at the airport.

senses.def: something that a person usually does
ex: It was his custom to walk along the river every evening.
As was her custom, she arrived ten minutes early.

senses.def: to put a dead body into the ground or a grave
ex: My grandfather is buried in his home village.
They buried the old cat under the apple tree.

senses.def: to put something in a hole in the ground and cover it
ex: Squirrels bury nuts to eat in winter.
The children buried a box of toys in the garden.

senses.def: to cover something completely so that it cannot be seen
ex: The village was buried under deep snow.
My keys were buried at the bottom of my bag.

senses.def: the railway as a way of travelling or of sending goods
ex: Most goods arrive at the port by rail.
The company offers cheap rail tickets for students.

senses.def: a bar fixed along a wall, stairs or balcony that you can hold or hang things on
ex: Hold the rail as you go down the stairs.
Hang your wet towel on the rail.

senses.def: one of the two metal bars that a train runs on
ex: The train came off the rails near the bridge.
Never walk along the rails; it is very dangerous.

senses.def: to say that you admire or approve of someone or something
ex: The coach praised the players for their hard work.
Critics have praised the film for its beautiful music.

senses.def: a feeling of great happiness
ex: She cried with joy when she heard the news.
The children jumped for joy when they saw the snow.

senses.def: a person or thing that gives you great happiness or pleasure
ex: Cooking with my grandmother was one of the joys of my childhood.
The little garden is her pride and joy.

senses.def: a story, often about imaginary or exciting events
ex: Grandpa loves telling tales about his years at sea.
The book is a moving tale of friendship and adventure.

senses.def: a report about someone’s bad behaviour, or a story that may not be true
ex: Don’t tell tales about your classmates to the teacher.
There are all sorts of wild tales about what happened that night.

senses.def: to control an activity or process by using official rules
ex: New laws will regulate the use of drones in cities.
The industry is strictly regulated by the government.

senses.def: to control the speed, temperature or amount of something so that it works well
ex: Sweating helps the body regulate its temperature.
This valve regulates the flow of water into the tank.

senses.def: a hard round vegetable that grows under the ground and is white inside
ex: Peel the potatoes, then boil them.
I’d like a baked potato, please.

senses.def: to use something such as fuel, energy or time
ex: Old fridges consume much more energy than new ones.
This project is consuming all my free time.

senses.def: to eat or drink something
ex: Adults should consume less salt and sugar.
Most of the food was consumed within an hour of the party starting.

senses.def: to buy and use goods and services
ex: Rich countries consume far more than they produce.
Young people consume most of their news on their phones.

senses.def: if a strong feeling consumes you, you cannot think about anything else
ex: After the argument, he was consumed with guilt.
She was consumed by the desire to win.

senses.def: the brother of your mother or father, or the husband of your aunt
ex: My uncle lives in the countryside.
My aunt and uncle taught me to swim.

senses.def: a material made from animal skin and used for making shoes, bags and clothes
ex: These shoes are made of real leather.
Leather usually lasts much longer than plastic.

senses.def: connected with a king or queen or a member of their family
ex: Millions of people watched the royal wedding on TV.
The royal family spends the summer at the palace by the sea.

senses.def: required by a rule or law, so that you have no choice
ex: Wearing a helmet is compulsory on building sites.
Maths is a compulsory subject until the age of sixteen.
pat: it is compulsory to do sth

senses.def: the basic systems a country or organization needs, such as roads, power and water supplies
ex: The country needs to invest more in its infrastructure.
Heavy floods damaged roads, bridges and other infrastructure in the region.

senses.def: an official who controls a game and makes sure the players obey the rules
ex: The referee blew the whistle to end the match.
The players argued with the referee about the penalty.

senses.def: (British English) a person who describes your character and abilities when you apply for a job
ex: Please give the names of two referees on your application form.
My former manager agreed to act as a referee for me.

senses.def: a thick tropical forest where it rains a lot during the year
ex: Many rare animals live only in the rainforest.
Huge areas of rainforest are cut down every year for farming.

senses.def: the way in which the sounds of a word or language are said
ex: Her pronunciation is very clear and easy to understand.
This app helps you practise your pronunciation every day.

senses.def: to live through a difficult or painful experience
ex: She went through a very difficult time after her father died.
Most teenagers go through periods of self-doubt.

senses.def: to look at or check something carefully, from beginning to end
ex: Let’s go through the answers together.
Customs officers went through all our bags at the border.

senses.def: to be accepted by a group because you are similar to the other people in it
ex: It took me a few months to fit in at my new job.
He never really fitted in with the other students.

senses.def: to find time to do something or to see someone
ex: The dentist can fit you in on Tuesday morning.
I try to fit in a short run before work.

senses.def: to learn something so well that you can say it from memory without looking
ex: We had to learn the whole poem by heart.
Actors must learn their lines by heart before rehearsals start.

senses.def: used to introduce a fact or opinion that is different from the one just mentioned
ex: On the one hand, the job pays well; on the other hand, the hours are long.
Small cars are cheap to run, but on the other hand, they aren’t very comfortable.
col: on the one hand ... on the other hand

senses.def: to take action so that all people are treated fairly and have the same chances
ex: New laws aim to promote equality between men and women at work.
The charity works to promote equality and diversity in sport.
pat: promote equality between sb and sb

senses.def: (British English, of a bathroom) joined directly to a bedroom and used only by the people in that room
ex: Every bedroom has an en suite shower room.
We booked a double room with an en suite bathroom.

notes.business#n: EVP-like A2 (business = buying and selling); A1 seems one level too low.
notes.lead#v: EVP-like B1 for most senses; only the basic "show the way" sense is plausibly A2.
notes.control#v: EVP-like B1; A2 looks slightly low for the verb.
notes.power#n: EVP-like B1 (both electricity and control senses); A2 looks low.
notes.law#n: EVP-like B1; A2 is borderline low.
notes.certain#adj: EVP-like B1 for both "sure" and "particular" senses; A2 looks low.
notes.much#adv: Current lexicon example "How much does this bag cost?" shows the determiner/pronoun use, not the adverb; replace it.
notes.material#n: EVP-like B1; A2 is borderline low.
notes.guess#v: EVP-like A2; A1 is borderline low.
notes.perfect#adj: EVP-like A2; A1 is borderline low.
notes.drug#n: EVP-like B1 for both the medicine and the illegal sense; A2 looks low.
notes.female#adj: EVP-like B1; A2 is borderline low.
notes.concert#n: EVP-like A2; A1 is borderline low.
notes.wed#v: Rare, mainly journalistic/literary; for learners it is closer to C1. B2 is generous, and the register should be shown as written.
notes.reserve#v: The "book a table/room" sense is EVP-like B1; B2 looks one level high.
notes.academic#adj: EVP-like B2 for the adjective; B1 is borderline low.
notes.honor#n: US spelling; British "honour" should be linked as a variant so learners find both.
notes.diet#n: EVP-like A2 (healthy diet) / B1 (on a diet); A1 looks low.
notes.salary#n: EVP-like B1; A2 is borderline low.
notes.chip#n: BrE "chips" (= AmE fries) and AmE "chips" (= BrE crisps) differ; both senses are given, with the regional label in the definition.
notes.regulate#v: EVP-like C1 for the verb; B2 looks one level low.
notes.consume#v: EVP-like B2 (use energy/eat); B1 looks one level low.
notes.infrastructure#n: EVP-like C1; B2 is borderline low.
notes.learn by heart#idiom: Common in classrooms from B1; B2 looks slightly high.
notes.promote equality#collocation: A collocation rather than a headword; consider listing it under promote#v (sense 2) instead of as a separate entry.
notes.en suite#adj: British English; also used as a noun ("a room with an en suite"). Label the region in the UI.
